first_lines: Table 1: Normal Reference range for basic laboratory investigations
Table 2: Event Timeline for patient 1, 2 and 3

rows: Presented to Emergency department with 1 week of fever, pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Covid -19 is diagnosed. Intubated in Emergency Department

Deprone 
Transthoracic echocardiogram does not demonstrate any structural, valvular or functional abnormalities.
Developed sinus bradycardia with heart rate mostly between 55-60.

Developed ACS with cardiogenic shock and then pulse ventricular tachycardia followed by Pulseless Electrical Activity (PEA) and asystole. Resuscitated as per ACLS protocol but patient remained asystole. Pronounced dead

Presented to Emergency Department with acute onset of shortness of breath of 3 days duration duration with severe hypoxic respiratory failure. Intubated in Emergency Department. Covid -19 is diagnosed.
Worsening PaO2/FiO2 ratio. Had Computed Tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) that showed extensive patchy peripheral ground-glass opacification throughout the thorax but no pulmonary embolism.
Developed oligouric acute kidney injury (AKI) and MAP < 60. Started on Noradrenaline.

Deteriorate to anuria AKI and started on Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT). Developed CHB requiring 2 inotropes. 
Temporary pacing wire inserted. Bedside echocardiography showed no pericardial effusion
Developed refractory hypoxemia with severe Pao2/FiO2 ratio. Chest Radiograph is not suggestive of pneumothorax. No pericardial effusion on Repeat bedside echocardiography
Family opted for Comfort measures. Patient passed away
Presented to Emergency Department acute onset of shortness of breath for 4 days duration associated with fever, myalgias and diarrhea. Covid -19 is diagnosed. Started on Non Invasive ventilation.
Intubated for worsening hypoxic respiratory failure. Underwent Lower Section Caesarean Section (LSCS). Proned immediately after.

Deprone. 
Map< 60. Started on noradrenaline. ECG, echocardiogram findings and laboratory investigations is suggestive of 
Myocarditis.
Developed CHB while in prone position.
Transferred to other Critical Care Centre for continuation of care
